name: Abbas
milestone_by_age_26: Got his first big break photographing the 1968 Mexico City Olympics for the International Olympic Committee at age 24, and by 1970 his major photojournalism works were being published in world magazines.
early_history_summary: Born in Iran and raised in Algeria during the war of independence, Abbas was self-taught in photography and relocated to Paris in the late 1960s. His first major assignment was covering the 1968 Mexico Olympics for the IOC, which launched his career as a conflict photojournalist covering Biafra, Vietnam, and South Africa in the 1970s.
family_context_summary: Born in Khash, Iran near the Pakistan border; family relocated to Algeria when he was a boy, where growing up during the war of independence sparked his interest in documenting political events. Little biographical information is available about his family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: political conflict exposure, self-taught, Paris photojournalism scene
evidence_summary: Abbas was a self-taught photographer who grew up in Algeria during its war of independence, which sparked his interest in documenting political conflict. He relocated to Paris in the late 1960s and got his first big break at the 1968 Mexico Olympics. By 1970 his work was being published in world magazines, and he joined Sipa Press in 1971. No evidence of family financial support, parental domain expertise, or formal training was found in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in 1944 in Khash, Iran; family relocated to Algeria when he was a boy, where growing up during the war of independence sparked his interest in documenting political events.
current_position: Died in April 2018 in Paris at age 74; was a renowned Magnum photographer known for documenting wars, revolutions, and religions worldwide.

trajectory.event: Got his first big break photographing the 1968 Mexico City Olympics for the International Olympic Committee.
Joined Sipa Press, beginning his professional photojournalism career in Paris.
Returned to Iran to photograph the Iranian Revolution, producing his most iconic work.
Joined Magnum Photos, becoming one of the agency's most prominent members.
Published 'Allah O Akbar,' a major photographic journey through militant Islam.
Died in Paris on April 25, 2018, while working on a project documenting Judaism.

name: Heinz-Harald Frentzen
milestone_by_age_26: Finished runner-up in the 1989 German Formula Three Championship at age 22 and was contracted to the Mercedes junior sportscar team alongside Michael Schumacher and Karl Wendlinger.
early_history_summary: Frentzen began karting at age 12 after his father, a former racing driver, bought him his first kart. He won the German Junior Kart Championship at 14, progressed through Formula Ford and Formula Three, and by 1989 was runner-up in German F3 and contracted to Mercedes' junior team, racing against Schumacher and Wendlinger.
family_context_summary: Born in Mönchengladbach, West Germany; father Heinrich-Harald was a German entrepreneur and former racing driver (1950-1957) who became a funeral director, mother Angela was Spanish. Parents divorced when he was eight. Father funded his karting career and acted as team boss and mechanic.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a racing driver from 1950 to 1957 and later a funeral director; he bought Frentzen his first kart at 12, funded his early career, and served as team boss and mechanic, providing direct domain expertise transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father racer, karting from age 12, Mercedes junior team, German motorsport ecosystem
evidence_summary: Frentzen benefited from a direct family-domain apprenticeship: his father was a former racing driver who bought him his first kart at 12, funded his career, and acted as team boss and mechanic. He won the German Junior Kart Championship at 14 and progressed rapidly through junior formulae. By 22 he was runner-up in German F3 and contracted to the Mercedes junior team alongside Schumacher. The West German motorsport ecosystem and proximity to the Kerpen track provided additional structural advantages.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Mönchengladbach, West Germany; father was a German entrepreneur and former racing driver (1950-1957) who became a funeral director, mother was Spanish; parents divorced when he was eight.
current_position: Former Formula One driver who competed from 1994 to 2003; runner-up in the 1997 F1 World Championship with Williams; resides in Monaco.

trajectory.event: Won the German Junior Kart Championship, beginning an extraordinarily successful karting career.
Finished runner-up in the German Formula Three Championship and was contracted to the Mercedes junior sportscar team alongside Schumacher and Wendlinger.
Made his Formula One debut with Sauber at the Brazilian Grand Prix.
Finished runner-up in the F1 World Championship with Williams, winning his maiden Grand Prix at Imola.
Achieved his best championship result with Jordan, finishing 3rd with two Grand Prix victories.
Retired from Formula One after a final season with Sauber.

name: Dragan Kićanović
milestone_by_age_26: Named MVP of the 1974 FIBA World Championship at age 21, having already won European Championship gold medals in 1973 and 1975 with the Yugoslav national team.
early_history_summary: Kićanović began playing basketball at age 13 in his hometown of Čačak, joining KK Železničar in 1966. He moved to Borac Čačak and then Partizan Belgrade in 1972, quickly becoming a key player for the dominant Yugoslav national team that won multiple European and World Championship medals throughout the 1970s.
family_context_summary: Born in Čačak, Yugoslavia; father Milan was a railway worker and mother Jovanka was a shopkeeper. He was an only child. His father brought home a membership card for KK Železničar Čačak when Dragan was three, connecting him to basketball early.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked on the railway and was connected to KK Železničar, the local basketball club, which he introduced to Dragan at age three. No evidence of parental basketball expertise, but the father facilitated early club access.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yugoslav basketball system, Partizan Belgrade, early club membership, national team
evidence_summary: Kićanović emerged from the Yugoslav basketball pipeline, one of the world's best development systems in the 1970s. His father, a railway worker, connected him to KK Železničar at age three, and coaches at the club nurtured his talent from age 13. He progressed to Partizan Belgrade at 19 and the national team at 20, where he was surrounded by elite peers. His working-class background provided no financial safety net, but the state-supported sports system compensated.
starting_point: Born in 1953 in Čačak, Yugoslavia; father was a railway worker and mother a shopkeeper; father connected him to basketball by bringing home a membership card for KK Železničar when he was three.
current_position: Retired basketball legend and FIBA Hall of Famer; served as Minister of Youth and Sports of Serbia (1991-1992) and President of the Olympic Committee of Serbia and Montenegro (1996-2005).

trajectory.event: Won European Championship gold with the Yugoslav national team, establishing himself on the international stage.
Named MVP of the FIBA World Championship in Puerto Rico.
Won Olympic silver medal with Yugoslavia at the Montreal Olympics.
Won the Yugoslav Cup and Korac Cup with Partizan Belgrade, cementing his status as a European club champion.
Won Olympic gold medal with Yugoslavia at the Moscow Olympics.
Named European Player of the Year (Mr. Europa and Euroscar) for the first time.
Inducted into the FIBA Hall of Fame in recognition of his international basketball career.

name: Yvonne Farrell
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Grafton Architects in 1977-78 at age 26-27, but no major buildings, awards, or independent recognition materialized until decades later (World Building of the Year 2008, Pritzker Prize 2020). Founding a firm is a career start, not a material milestone.
early_history_summary: Farrell studied architecture at University College Dublin, graduating in 1974, and began teaching there in 1976. She co-founded Grafton Architects with Shelley McNamara in 1977-78, but the practice's major acclaim came much later with the Bocconi University building (2008) and the Pritzker Prize (2020).
family_context_summary: Born in Tullamore, County Offaly, Ireland; attended school with nuns who supported her interest in architecture. Little documented about family financial background.
evidence_summary: Farrell graduated from UCD in 1974 and co-founded Grafton Architects in 1977-78, but her major architectural achievements (World Building of the Year 2008, RIBA International Prize 2016, Pritzker Prize 2020) all came decades after age 26. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Boris Gromov
milestone_by_age_26: Commissioned as a Soviet Army officer in 1965 at age 22, but no material military milestone by age 26; his significant commands and Hero of the Soviet Union award came during the Afghan War in the 1980s.
early_history_summary: Gromov graduated from the Suvorov Military School in 1962 and was commissioned from the Leningrad Higher Combined Arms Command School in 1965. He held junior command assignments through his twenties, with his career-defining achievements coming during three tours in Afghanistan in the 1980s.
family_context_summary: Born in Saratov into a working-class family; father was killed fighting Nazi invaders when Boris was a few months old. Raised by his mother.
evidence_summary: Gromov was commissioned as a Soviet Army officer in 1965 at age 22, but his career-defining achievements (commanding the 40th Army in Afghanistan, Hero of the Soviet Union, leading the Soviet withdrawal) all came in the 1980s when he was in his forties. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Björn Kuipers
milestone_by_age_26: Was an amateur referee by age 26; his professional refereeing debut came in 2002 at age 29, and his FIFA badge in 2006 at age 33. No material milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Kuipers began refereeing at 16 after his father, also a referee, challenged him to try it. He became an amateur referee for the KNVB in 1990 but spent over a decade in amateur ranks. His professional debut came in 2002, and he rose to FIFA and UEFA Elite status in the late 2000s.
family_context_summary: Born in Oldenzaal, Netherlands; father Jan was a referee and supermarket owner who directed Björn toward refereeing at age 16. Kuipers later took over the family supermarket business.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a referee and supermarket owner who encouraged Björn to take up refereeing at 16, providing direct domain exposure. The family supermarket business (since 1937) provided a financial platform.
evidence_summary: Kuipers started refereeing at 16 after his father's challenge, but his professional debut did not come until 2002 at age 29, and his FIFA badge in 2006 at age 33. By age 26 he was an amateur referee with no material milestone. His major achievements (Champions League final 2014, Euro 2020 final) all came in his late thirties and forties.

name: Héctor Lombard
milestone_by_age_26: Represented Cuba at the 2000 Sydney Olympics in the lightweight judo division at age 22, competing at the highest level of international judo as a fourth-degree black belt.
early_history_summary: Born in Matanzas, Cuba, Lombard trained in judo within the Cuban national sports system, achieving a fourth-degree black belt and earning selection to represent Cuba at the 2000 Sydney Olympics. He later transitioned to mixed martial arts, beginning his professional MMA career around 2004.
family_context_summary: Born in Matanzas, Cuba; little documented about family background. He trained in judo within the Cuban national sports system and later emigrated to Australia and then the United States.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban sports system, Olympic judo, martial arts training
evidence_summary: Lombard emerged from the Cuban national sports system, which identified and developed his judo talent to Olympic level by age 22. Little is documented about his family background or early training specifics. The Cuban state-supported athletic pipeline provided structured training, though financial resources were limited. His later transition to MMA and defection from Cuba added an adversity dimension to his career trajectory.
starting_point: Born in 1978 in Matanzas, Cuba; little documented about family background; trained in judo within the Cuban national sports system.
current_position: Cuban-Australian professional mixed martial artist and former Olympic judoka; last competed in Eagle FC; resides in Coconut Creek, Florida.

trajectory.event: Represented Cuba in judo at the Sydney Olympics in the lightweight division.
Began his professional mixed martial arts career, transitioning from judo to MMA.
Won the inaugural Bellator Middleweight Championship.
Made his UFC debut, signing with the premier MMA promotion.
Fought his last UFC bout against Thales Leites before moving to Eagle FC.

name: Enith Brigitha
milestone_by_age_26: Won silver in the 200m backstroke at the 1973 inaugural FINA World Championships at age 18, and later won two bronze medals at the 1976 Montreal Olympics at age 21, becoming the first black athlete to win an Olympic swimming medal.
early_history_summary: Born in Curaçao, Brigitha learned to swim in the Caribbean Sea and became the island's most promising swimmer. Her divorced mother moved the family to the Netherlands around 1970 so Enith could train seriously under coach Willie Storm at Club Het Y in Amsterdam. She qualified for the 1972 Olympics at 17 and quickly became the dominant Dutch swimmer of the 1970s.
family_context_summary: Born in Willemstad, Curaçao; eldest daughter of a Dutch mother and an Antillean father. Parents divorced. Her mother moved with Enith and her brother to the Netherlands around 1970 to support Enith's swimming career, a significant family sacrifice.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of parental swimming expertise. However, the mother's decision to relocate from Curaçao to the Netherlands specifically to support Enith's swimming career represents significant family domain support.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Dutch swimming system, mother's support, coach Willie Storm, Caribbean swimming roots
evidence_summary: Brigitha's early advantage came from her mother's decision to relocate from Curaçao to the Netherlands to support her swimming career, combined with access to coach Willie Storm at Club Het Y in Amsterdam. She learned to swim in the Caribbean Sea as a child, giving her early domain immersion. As a black swimmer from a small island in a white-dominated sport, she faced structural barriers but also had the drive of an outsider. Her talent was evident early as she became Curaçao's most promising swimmer before her teens.
starting_point: Born in 1955 in Willemstad, Curaçao; eldest daughter of a Dutch mother and an Antillean father; parents divorced; mother moved with her to the Netherlands around 1970 to support her swimming career.
current_position: Retired competitive swimmer; owns a swimming school for children; moved back to Curaçao in 1990 before returning to the Netherlands.

trajectory.event: Qualified for the Munich Olympics, reaching the final in four events including 100m freestyle.
Won silver in the 200m backstroke and bronze in the 100m freestyle at the inaugural FINA World Championships in Belgrade.
Won five medals at the European Championships and was named Dutch Sportswoman of the Year for the second consecutive year.
Won two bronze medals at the Montreal Olympics in the 100m and 200m freestyle, becoming the first black athlete to win an Olympic swimming medal.
Won her seventh consecutive Dutch 100m freestyle title, capping a dominant domestic career.
Moved back to Curaçao and opened her own swimming school for children.

name: Enya
milestone_by_age_26: Released her debut solo album 'Enya' (soundtrack for the BBC series 'The Celts') in March 1987 at age 25, which reached #8 on the Irish Albums Chart and #69 on the UK Albums Chart.
early_history_summary: Born into the musically prominent Brennan family in Gweedore, Ireland, Enya began piano at age 4 and singing competitions at age 3. She joined her siblings' band Clannad at 19 in 1980, left in 1982, and spent four years developing her distinctive multi-tracked vocal sound with producer Nicky Ryan and lyricist Roma Ryan in their garden shed studio before being commissioned by the BBC in 1985.
family_context_summary: Born in Dore, Gweedore, County Donegal, Ireland; sixth of nine children in the musically prominent Brennan family. Father Leo led an Irish showband (Slieve Foy) and owned Leo's Tavern. Mother Baba was a teacher and amateur musician. Grandfather was a pianist and entertainer; grandmother was a professional singer and percussionist. Boarding school from age 11 paid for by grandfather.
parent_family_domain_summary: Deep multi-generational musical family: father was a showband leader and pub owner, mother was a music teacher and amateur musician, grandfather was a pianist/entertainer, grandmother was a professional singer. Siblings formed the internationally successful band Clannad. The family pub, Leo's Tavern, was a live music venue.
primary_early_advantage_tags: musical family, Clannad, Nicky Ryan partnership, BBC commission, Celtic music culture
evidence_summary: Enya's early advantage was deeply rooted in her family's musical heritage across multiple generations. Her father's showband and pub provided constant live music immersion from childhood, while her mother's music teaching gave her formal piano training from age 4. Joining Clannad at 19 gave her professional touring and recording experience. The complementary partnership with Nicky and Roma Ryan was essential—they built a studio in their garden shed and developed her signature sound over four years. The BBC commission for 'The Celts' in 1985 provided the breakthrough opportunity.
starting_point: Born in 1961 in Dore, Gweedore, County Donegal, Ireland; sixth of nine children in the musically prominent Brennan family; father Leo led an Irish showband and owned Leo's Tavern, mother Baba was a teacher and amateur musician.
current_position: Ireland's best-selling solo artist and one of the world's best-selling musical artists with over 80 million records sold; resides in a castle in Killiney, County Dublin; estimated net worth approximately $140 million.

trajectory.event: Joined the family band Clannad as keyboardist and backing vocalist at the invitation of producer Nicky Ryan.
Left Clannad to pursue a solo career, moving in with producer Nicky Ryan and lyricist Roma Ryan to develop her sound.
Released her debut solo album 'Enya' (soundtrack for the BBC series 'The Celts'), which reached #8 in Ireland and #69 in the UK.
Released 'Watermark' featuring the hit single 'Orinoco Flow,' which sold 8 million copies worldwide and launched her as an international star.
Released 'Shepherd Moons,' which won the Grammy Award for Best New Age Album and sold over 10 million copies.
Released 'A Day Without Rain,' featuring 'Only Time,' which became a global phenomenon after the September 11 attacks.
Released 'And Winter Came,' her final major studio album before an extended hiatus.

name: Joep Lange
milestone_by_age_26: Was a medical student at the University of Amsterdam, receiving his MD in 1981 at age 27; his pioneering HIV/AIDS research career began in the mid-1980s. No material milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Lange studied medicine at the University of Amsterdam, receiving his MD in 1981 and PhD in 1987. He was a foreign exchange student in the US from 1971 to 1972. His career-defining work in HIV/AIDS research began in the 1980s, leading to his role as president of the International AIDS Society (2002-2004).
family_context_summary: Born in Nieuwenhagen, Netherlands; was a Youth for Understanding exchange student in the US (1971-1972). Little documented about family financial background.
evidence_summary: Lange was still a medical student at the University of Amsterdam at age 26, receiving his MD in 1981 at age 27. His pioneering HIV/AIDS research, including early antiretroviral therapy trials and prevention of mother-to-child transmission, began in the mid-1980s. His major leadership roles (IAS president, PharmAccess Foundation founder) came even later. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Peter O'Toole
milestone_by_age_26: Made his West End debut in 'The Long and the Short and the Tall' at the Royal Court in January 1959 at age 26, winning Best Actor of the Year and attracting the attention of director David Lean.
early_history_summary: O'Toole left school at 14, worked as a journalist, served in the Royal Navy, then attended RADA on scholarship from 1952 to 1954 alongside Richard Harris, Alan Bates, and Albert Finney. He spent several years at the Bristol Old Vic as a Shakespearean actor before his breakthrough West End role in 1959.
family_context_summary: Born in Leeds, son of a Scottish nurse and an Irish metal plater, football player, and bookmaker. Grew up in the working-class suburb of Hunslet. Left school at 14. No family financial platform or domain connections to acting.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of parental connection to acting or the arts. Father was a metal plater and bookmaker; mother was a nurse. The family traveled around Northern English racecourse towns.
primary_early_advantage_tags: RADA scholarship, Bristol Old Vic, English Stage Company, working-class drive
evidence_summary: O'Toole's early advantage came primarily from institutional access: a scholarship to RADA, one of the world's most elite drama schools, where he studied alongside future stars Harris, Bates, and Finney. He then honed his craft at the Bristol Old Vic, a prestigious repertory theatre. His working-class background and unconventional path (leaving school at 14, Navy service, journalism) provided drive but no financial safety net. His extraordinary natural talent was recognized early, with critics predicting greatness from his earliest stage appearances.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Leeds, England; son of a Scottish nurse and an Irish metal plater/bookmaker; grew up in the working-class suburb of Hunslet; left school at 14 to work as a journalist.
current_position: Died in December 2013 in London at age 81; was one of the most celebrated actors of the 20th century, known for Lawrence of Arabia and eight Oscar nominations.

trajectory.event: Graduated from RADA and began working in theatre, making his television debut in The Scarlet Pimpernel.
Joined the Bristol Old Vic as a Shakespearean actor, appearing in King Lear, Othello, and Major Barbara.
Made his West End debut in 'The Long and the Short and the Tall' at the Royal Court, winning Best Actor of the Year.
Starred as the title character in David Lean's 'Lawrence of Arabia,' receiving his first Oscar nomination and achieving international stardom.
Played the title role in Hamlet for the National Theatre's inaugural production.
Received an Academy Honorary Award for lifetime achievement in film.
Died on December 14, 2013, in London after a long illness.

name: Marwan al-Shehhi
milestone_by_age_26: Committed the terrorist act of hijacking United Airlines Flight 175 and crashing it into the South Tower of the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001, at age 23. This was an act of mass murder, not a positive achievement or success milestone.
early_history_summary: Al-Shehhi was born in Ras al Khaimah, UAE, the son of a mosque prayer leader. He received a military scholarship to study in Germany in 1996, where he met Mohamed Atta and joined the Hamburg cell. He attended flight school in Florida in 2000 before carrying out the 9/11 attacks.
family_context_summary: Born in Ras al Khaimah, UAE; father was a prayer leader at the local mosque who died in 1997. Family lived in the run-down Qusaibat settlement. Al-Shehhi received a military scholarship to study in Germany.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a muezzin (prayer leader) at the local mosque. No evidence of domain expertise relevant to any constructive career.
evidence_summary: Al-Shehhi's only notable act was the terrorist hijacking of United Airlines Flight 175 on September 11, 2001, which was an act of mass murder rather than a constructive achievement. This does not qualify as a success milestone. He was a university student in Germany who became radicalized through the Hamburg cell alongside Mohamed Atta.
